title: Finite Kan arrow diagrams lift simultaneously above their stage
statement: Let J be a small filtered category and F:J→Cat a diagram of small categories [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let V be a cocone whose object and arrow cocones are colimits of sets [def-weil-pbc-arrows-functor]. Fix i in J, t=(i→j) in Under(i), and U in F(j). Put L=V_j^op and D=CostructuredArrow(L,L(U^op)); an object p of D consists of W_p in F(j) and an arrow f_p:V_j(U)→V_j(W_p). A morphism h:p→q has underlying arrow h^unop:W_q→W_p with f_q followed by V_j(h^unop)=f_p. Let S be any finite set of objects of D containing p₀=(U,id), and T any finite set of morphisms of D (encoded together with their endpoints). Then there exist r in Under(i), b:t→r, and for every p in S an arrow g_p:F(b.right)(U)→F(b.right)(W_p), such that g_q followed by F(b.right)(h^unop)=g_p whenever p,q lie in S and h:p→q belongs to T, and g_p₀=id. No section or presheaf is part of this assertion; morphisms of T with an endpoint outside S impose no equation.

source.place: Tag 0A35 (lemma-compute-pullback-to-limit), omitted independence-of-presentation verification; Categories, Section Tag 04AX, eventual equality in filtered set colimits

proof.text: Represent each f_p in the arrow colimit by joint surjectivity. Choose common later stages receiving j and each representative stage, then use IsFiltered.wideSpan on the maps out of j to obtain one stage k and one map c:j→k for the entire finite family. Cocone naturality identifies the images of these representatives with the original arrows.

For each p, the source of its representative has the same object-colimit image as F(c)(U), and its target has the same image as F(c)(W_p). Apply same-stage eventual equality to this finite family indexed by S×Bool. Synchronize all resulting maps out of k using IsFiltered.wideSpan, obtaining d:k→l where both endpoint equalities hold for every p. Transport each arrow along these equalities, obtaining g_p from F(d)F(c)(U) to F(d)F(c)(W_p). Transport does not change its Arrow image.

Restrict the finite edge set T to edges whose endpoints belong to S. For each such h:p→q compare the entire arrows g_q followed by F(d)F(c)(h^unop) and g_p. Their Arrow images agree by the costructured-arrow triangle, cocone naturality, and preservation of composition. Also compare g_p₀ with the identity. Its Arrow image is the identity by construction. Apply same-stage eventual equality in the arrow colimit to this finite family of comparisons, indexed by the restricted edge set plus one distinguished identity comparison. Synchronize with wideSpan, obtaining a:l→m where all equations hold.

Let v=c followed by d followed by a, r=Under.mk(t.hom followed by v), and b=Under.homMk(v). Transport the arrows F(a)(g_p) along the object equalities supplied by F.map_comp. Functor.congr_hom transports each transition arrow consistently, so the triangle equations just established persist; the identity comparison gives g_p₀=id. The common map v makes the Under triangle hold without a separate equalization out of i. Finite-family constructions include the case of an empty edge set.

from.place: Step 2 of lem-weil-pbc-colimit-site-kan-unit-relations: lift the finite Kan relation diagram and its identity endpoint at one refinement. The existing ancestor chain stops at a module name.

lean.statement: theorem colimit_site_finite_kan_arrow_lift (J : Type u) [SmallCategory J] [IsFiltered J] (F : J ⥤ Cat.{u, u}) (V : Cocone F) (hobjects : IsColimit (Cat.objects.mapCocone V)) (harrows : IsColimit (Cat.arrows.mapCocone V)) (i : J) (t : Under i) (U : F.obj t.right) : let L := (V.ι.app t.right).toFunctor.op let D := CostructuredArrow L (L.obj (op U)) ∀ (S : Finset D) (T : Finset (Σ p q : D, p ⟶ q)) (hunit : CostructuredArrow.mk (𝟙 (L.obj (op U))) ∈ S), ∃ (r : Under i) (b : t ⟶ r) (g : ∀ p : S, (F.map b.right).toFunctor.obj U ⟶ (F.map b.right).toFunctor.obj p.val.left.unop), (∀ (p q : S) (h : p.val ⟶ q.val), ⟨p.val, q.val, h⟩ ∈ T → g q ≫ (F.map b.right).toFunctor.map h.left.unop = g p) ∧ g ⟨CostructuredArrow.mk (𝟙 (L.obj (op U))), hunit⟩ = 𝟙 _
